request:
I run a small provisions shop in Madina and I want to keep my price list on the computer instead of in my notebook. I want to add the things I sell with their prices. I want to see everything I sell, and look up the price of one thing. Sometimes I stop selling something, so I want to take it off the list.

The client's answers to your questions:
Q: Do you sell some things by different sizes or units, like a tin, a sachet or a carton of the same item, and should each one have its own price?
A: No preference: you decide.
Q: When your prices change, do you want to edit the price of an item already on the list, or just remove it and add it again?
A: Yes, prices change all the time, especially sugar, rice and oil. I need to change the price of an item.
Q: When you stop selling something, should it disappear completely, or do you want to keep it somewhere in case you sell it again later?
A: It is gone: it does not show in the list and looking it up says it is not found.

Where the client has no preference or did not answer, choose the simplest option and add nothing they did not ask for (no logins, PINs or extra required fields).
summary:
I wrote `app.py` and the tests in `tests/test_app.py` pass. Prices are stored in a SQLite file called `shop.db`, which is created when the app starts.

- `POST /items` adds an item. Send `{"name": "...", "price": ...}`. It returns the new item with its `id`. A blank name, a missing price or a negative price is refused with a 422 error.
- `GET /items` lists everything you sell.
- `GET /items/{id}` gives one item and its price. It returns 404 if the item isn't there.
- `PUT /items/{id}` changes the price of an item. Send `{"price": ...}`. It returns 404 if the item isn't there.
- `DELETE /items/{id}` removes an item for good. Afterwards it no longer shows in the list, and looking it up returns 404.

I treated each size or unit as its own item, for example "Sugar sachet" and "Sugar carton", since you had no preference.
